items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1965-09-13
items.q: When I got there, Von Gammon, the leader of the band, says, what are you doing with that, homin?

ctx.x: Right. Did all this extracurricular activity bump into your schooling and did you have to quit

or did you carry on? Well, that's right. I gave up. I was going to Warren Eastern High School at the time and found out that I couldn't quite make it. So I said, well, I knew right then and there, I said, there's only one thing for me, that's music. I had no desire to learn anything else but just to play music. Now you asked me about some musicians. Here was a place where I began meeting the old Real Dixieland musicians. For instance, we had a drummer playing there by the name, he replaced the fellow that really…

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: The drummer was Von Gammon at the time I went there. He was the leader.

ctx.x: Can you just mention a few of the names?

Oh, yes. I remember, for sure, they had... Broken Dishes. Von Gammon. Oh, well, he's talking about my girlfriend now. Broken... I'm just kidding. She could have been. Broken Dishes, who really used to be a real tough girl. She used to beat up all the other girls, you know. She was tattooed. She was tattooed from head to foot. You know, the girls were working on tickets, you know. They'd try to beat one another out of dances, and she'd go back in, and she'd have it out with them. But it was all really part of the…

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: It was Von Gammon's band, the drummer.

ctx.x: Whose band was it at the Fern, anyway?
It was Von Gammon's band, the drummer.
And what other bands did Gillen play with that you know of?
